items.desc: Our hero at a desk, back to us, framed by a huge window. Lightning splits the night sky over the city. On the laptop screen, in red: "APPRAISAL: MEETS EXPECTATIONS (3%)". Reflected in the window, faintly: Captain Quick-Call's smile.
items.tagline: NOTICE PERIOD #1 · THE LAST STRAW · price tag: ₹0 · NO HIKE.

panels.label: wide
panels.desc: Night. A glass tower lit up on its 14th floor. A giant logo: an infinity symbol that looks a bit like a handcuff.

lines.text: Synergex Solutions Pvt Ltd. Mission statement: "Synergising tomorrow, today."
Nobody knows what it means. Nobody has asked since 2014.
slow pan up the tower.

panels.desc: A small rented flat. {HERO} on the sofa in shorts, eating instant noodles straight from the pan, a show paused on TV.

lines.text: Sunday. 11:58 PM. The last free two minutes of the week.

panels.label: close-up
panels.desc: The phone on the cushion lights up {HERO}'s face blue.

lines.text: PING!
small shake.
Got 5 mins? 🙂
The smiley was the scariest part.

panels.desc: {HERO}'s thumb hovers.

lines.text: It was not 5 minutes. It was a "small thing". It was not small.
Monday-morning {HERO} would pay for this.

panels.desc: Either way: {HERO} lying in bed, eyes open, ceiling fan turning.

lines.text: Fourteen months. Fourteen months of "got 5 mins".

panels.label: wide
panels.desc: Monday. A glass meeting room called "INNOVATE" (the sign is peeling). Captain Quick-Call stands at a screen showing a slide titled YOUR GROWTH JOURNEY 🚀. First look at him: crisp shirt, lanyard like a medal, a smile with too many teeth, a phone permanently in one hand.

lines.text: {HERO}. You've been outstanding this year. Truly. The Phoenix fixes. The weekend work. The attitude.

panels.desc: He clicks to the next slide. A single word, huge: MEETS EXPECTATIONS.

lines.text: SKRRRT

panels.desc: Close on {HERO}, blinking.

lines.text: ...and a 3% hike.
My rent went up twelve.
Think of it as an investment. In your patience.

panels.desc: Back at the desk. Captain Quick-Call drops a printed copy of the appraisal on {HERO}'s keyboard. Then a second copy, "for your records". Then a third, "for HR".

lines.text: Sign all three. Physically. We're old school about feedback.

panels.label: close-up
panels.desc: {HERO} crumples the first copy into a tight ball. Across the aisle, past the Yes-Men's desks, sits the office bin. A desk fan creaks back and forth.

lines.text: Some people meditate. {HERO} had a bin and ten printouts.
KRRRNCH

items.title: THE BIN
items.intro: Ten printouts. One bin. One office fan that hates you.

lines.text: Paper everywhere. Admin sends an all-staff email: "Reminder: Clean Desk Policy". It is very clearly about {HERO}.
Most of them land. One bounces off the rim and rolls under Captain Quick-Call's chair. He doesn't notice. Yet.
Nothing but bin. A Yes-Man looks up, almost impressed.
First thing I've finished here in months.

panels.desc: The open office. A huge TV on the wall shows THE OVERLORD, the CEO: a giant, glowing head, filmed from below like a statue.

lines.text: RECORD PROFITS THIS YEAR, FAMILY!
The Overlord. Nobody has seen him in person. Some say he's a hologram. Some say he chose to be.

panels.desc: Below the TV, THE YES-MEN: four identical men in identical blue shirts, clapping in perfect sync.

lines.text: CLAP. CLAP. CLAP. CLAP.
Love that for us.

panels.desc: {HERO} at their desk, not clapping. A Yes-Man turns his head slowly, owl-like, to look at them.

panels.label: wide
panels.desc: The canteen. Steam everywhere. CHAI UNCLE behind the counter: 60s, sleeves rolled, a moustache with its own personality, pouring chai from a great height in one long golden arc.

lines.text: SHHHHHHH
Third cutting today. Appraisal?

panels.desc: {HERO} nods into the glass.

lines.text: Twenty-two years I've poured tea here. Every year, same tea, same story. Only the sugar changes.

panels.desc: Chai Uncle taps {HERO}'s phone, face-up on the counter. A LinkedIn-style post (fictional app, "Linkd") glows like a holy relic: "Thrilled to announce I'm starting a new position at...". The profile picture: THE ESCAPEE, a former colleague, beaming, with a halo of light.

lines.text: That one also used to drink three a day.

panels.label: flashback, sepia, rough edges
panels.desc: Two years ago. A sad farewell in a meeting room: one samosa each, a card signed "All the best!!" The Escapee leans in to a younger {HERO}.

lines.text: Don't wait for the perfect moment to leave. There isn't one in this building.

panels.desc: Back to now. {HERO} looks at the post, then at the canteen clock: 6:41 PM.

lines.text: Some people never forget their first chai. {HERO} would never forget this one.

panels.desc: {HERO}'s desk, 6:47 PM. Half the floor is empty. A SynChat notification slides in.

lines.text: Before you leave, small thing. Leadership wants the Phoenix deck "more punchy". By 9 AM? 🙂

panels.label: close-up
panels.desc: {HERO}'s eye. A tiny reflection of the 🙂 in their pupil.

lines.text: slow zoom.

panels.desc: Outside the window, lightning. The coffee mug on the desk, which says "WORLD'S OKAYEST EMPLOYEE", cracks down the middle.

lines.text: KRAK.
Every origin story has a moment...

panels.label: SPLASH
panels.desc: {HERO} stands. Their chair rolls away behind them. The lanyard swings mid-air. Every head on the floor turns. The light from the window turns {HERO} into a silhouette. Huge, hand-lettered across the page: Small inset panel: a Yes-Man drops his coffee.

lines.text: I QUIT.
...where the hero stops asking for permission.
DAY 1.
KLANG.
hold, then a slight shake on "I QUIT".

panels.desc: Silence. Everyone staring. {HERO} slowly picks the chair back up and sits down.

lines.text: ...I mean. I'm going to quit. Formally.
By email.

panels.desc: The Yes-Men go back to typing in perfect sync.

lines.text: Even revolutions need a subject line.

panels.desc: A blank email on {HERO}'s screen. To: Captain Quick-Call. Cc: HR. Subject: Resignation. The cursor blinks. {HERO}'s fingers hover. Their fingers are shaking with fourteen months of feelings.

items.title: THE DRAFT
items.intro: Your feelings are typing. HR is reading. Tap the angry words before they hit SEND.

lines.text: The raw email goes out. Inset: Madame Policy's eyes narrowing behind her glasses.
HR filed it under "Feedback (Hostile)."
The email is almost perfect, apart from one line that slipped through: "...and I am grateful for the circus." Inset: a Yes-Man reading it, eyebrows raised.
The final email appears in full: perfect, polite fury. A tiny inset: Madame Policy's hand stamps it TONE: COMPLIANT.

panels.desc: {HERO}'s finger on the SEND button.

lines.text: CLICK.

panels.label: wide
panels.desc: The email shoots across the floor as a glowing paper plane, weaving over cubicles. Heads follow it.

lines.text: WHOOOOSH

panels.desc: The plane lands on Captain Quick-Call's screen. His eye twitches.

lines.text: tik.

panels.desc: Ten seconds later. {HERO}'s phone.

lines.text: PING!
Got 5 mins?
Of course.

panels.desc: A split panel: {HERO} on a video call on the left, Captain Quick-Call filling the screen on the right. A clock in the corner: 0:01.

lines.text: Let's not be hasty.

panels.desc: Clock: 0:09.

lines.text: Sleep on it.
I've slept on it for fourteen months.

panels.desc: Clock: 0:23.

lines.text: We're a family here, {HERO}.
Then I'd like my share of the property.

panels.desc: Clock: 0:31. He's now drawing a diagram of "the bigger picture" on a whiteboard behind him.

lines.text: Minute thirty-one. He had not yet reached his point.

panels.label: close-up
panels.desc: {HERO}'s finger on the MUTE icon. It glows like a power-up.

lines.text: bwoop.
And so our hero discovered their first superpower.
Mute.

panels.desc: {HERO} leans back. In the air beside the screen, an imaginary dartboard fades into view. In its centre: Captain Quick-Call's face, still talking.

lines.text: ...growth mindset... long-term thinking... who will handle Q4...

items.title: THE QUICK CALL
items.intro: 47 minutes. You're on mute. Nobody will ever know.

lines.text: {HERO} laughs at their own miss and realises they're not muted.
...Is something funny, {HERO}?
Same, but {HERO} has to unmute twice because the first time it doesn't work.
No. ...NO.
Clock: 0:47.
Great chat! So you'll stay? {HERO} unmutes.
No.
bwip.

panels.desc: Captain Quick-Call, unbothered, smiling again.

lines.text: Fine. Fill the separation form on the portal. HR will guide you.
She's... very thorough.

panels.desc: The call ends. {HERO}'s screen goes dark. In the black reflection, behind {HERO}'s shoulder, a figure is standing perfectly still.

panels.label: SPLASH (villain introduction)
panels.desc: MADAME POLICY. Tall, immaculate, half-moon glasses on a chain, a cardigan worn like armour. Laminated policy pages orbit her like shields. A stamp in one hand, a pen in the other, neither ever put down. A villain card in the corner, trading-card style:

lines.text: Policy. Is. Policy.
She had not read the policy since 2009. Nobody had. It was safer that way.

card: Powers: Policy Shield · Form in Triplicate · "As Per Process"
Weakness: "Can you show me where it says that?"

panels.desc: {HERO} opens the HR portal, SynergexOne. A spinner turns.

lines.text: Loading your journey...

panels.desc: A homepage with 47 tiles: "My Journey", "My Wellbeing", "My Learning", "My Recognition (0)". There's no "Resign" anywhere.

lines.text: It's in there. Somewhere. As per process.
The session times out on the very last screen.
{HERO} filled the form three times. HR received all three.
Same button, but the form asks for the reason in a drop-down: Better opportunity / Personal reasons / Higher studies.
There's no option for "Manager". → they pick Personal reasons. No meter change.
{HERO} reaches the button in one run. A trumpet fanfare. The button reads: "Are you sure? (Your Synergex family will miss you 😢)". {HERO} taps YES without blinking.

panels.desc: A confirmation banner on screen: "Your resignation is PENDING APPROVAL."

lines.text: ...Quitting needs approval?

panels.desc: A calendar on {HERO}'s desk. Big red text appears across it.

lines.text: DAY 3. Notice period: 90 days. Remaining: 87.

panels.desc: The canteen, evening. Chai Uncle wipes a glass without looking up.

lines.text: The first three days are the easy ones.

panels.desc: {HERO} at the desk, packing up. A long shadow falls across them.

lines.text: slow zoom out.

panels.desc: Captain Quick-Call leans on the cubicle wall. His smile is wider than physically possible.

lines.text: Since you're leaving anyway...

panels.label: close-up
panels.desc: A fat, dusty folder slams onto the desk. On it, stencilled in red: PROJECT PHOENIX. Dust clouds rise.

lines.text: THUD.
...you won't mind owning this. Due Friday.

panels.desc: {HERO}'s face. The panel border cracks down the middle.

lines.text: TO BE CONTINUED IN ISSUE #2: "THE SQUEEZE"

items.desc: {HERO} buried up to the neck in a mountain of calendar invites. On top of the mountain stand the four Yes-Men, nodding, each holding a "Quick Sync" invite like a flag.
items.tagline: NOTICE PERIOD #2 · THE SQUEEZE · tagline: "Since you're leaving anyway..."

panels.label: "Previously" box, comic-style, with thumbnails of Issue #1

lines.text: PREVIOUSLY: {HERO} quit. Captain Quick-Call smiled. HR made it a maze. And then, a folder.

panels.desc: {HERO} opens the Phoenix folder. Dust. A slide deck: 412 slides. File name: Phoenix_FINAL_v9_USE THIS ONE.pptx.

lines.text: DAY 4. Project Phoenix: a system nobody understands, that everyone depends on, that nobody has touched since...

panels.label: close-up
panels.desc: The "Last edited by" line: THE ESCAPEE · 2 years ago.

lines.text: ...since the last person who escaped.

panels.desc: The Yes-Men gather around {HERO}'s desk in formation, laptops open, smiling identically.

lines.text: Since you own Phoenix now...
...we've set up a few syncs.
Just to align.
On the alignment.

panels.desc: {HERO}'s calendar. Invites flood in so fast they overflow the screen and spill onto the desk as physical cards.

lines.text: PING PING PING PING PING PING
shake, building up.

items.title: CALENDAR CARNAGE
items.intro: Your calendar is under attack. Defend your afternoon.

lines.text: {HERO} in a meeting room at 7 PM, the last one left. The cleaner turns off the lights on them.
A half-full calendar.
{HERO} attended four meetings about Phoenix. Phoenix was discussed in none of them.
{HERO}'s calendar shows one clean, glowing block: "Focus time". A Yes-Man stares at it like it's sorcery.

panels.desc: A Yes-Man leans over the partition, holding a cheerful poster: "OPTIONAL Team Outing! Saturday, 8 AM, Trekking 🥾".

lines.text: It's optional. (He doesn't blink.)
Inset: {HERO} on a hill at 8 AM, holding a team-building rope, dead inside.
Inset: {HERO} asleep until noon. On Monday a Yes-Man silently places a photo of the team on the hill on their desk.

panels.label: wide
panels.desc: Night. {HERO}'s flat. The city through the window. A laptop open on a job portal (fictional: "JobJunction").

lines.text: By day, Phoenix. By night, the Hunt.

panels.desc: A stats box on the portal: Applied: 47 · Viewed: 3 · Replied: 0.

lines.text: Forty-seven. That's not a job search. That's a lottery with extra steps.

panels.desc: The phone rings: an unknown number. {HERO} answers. The panel goes dark except for a silhouette in a trench coat, backlit by a city skyline. This is THE RECRUITER. Only their eyes and a headset mic are lit.

lines.text: Hello, am I speaking to {HERO}? Quick question.
Are you... an immediate joiner?

panels.desc: {HERO}, hopeful.

lines.text: I've already resigned! I can join in—
Ah. You resigned. Without an offer.
...Why? Is something wrong with you?

panels.desc: The silhouette fades.

lines.text: I'll keep your profile on file.
click.
Nobody has ever returned from "on file".

panels.desc: {HERO} stares at the screen. Then at the city skyline full of lit-up offices. They crack their knuckles.

lines.text: Fine. Then I'll go to all of you.

items.title: APPLY-O-MATIC
items.intro: Every lit window is a company. Every CV is a shot. Mind the black hole.

lines.text: One building lights up, then immediately goes dark. Notification: "Position closed."
A handful of windows lit.
Some days the Hunt is a sprint. Most days it's a slingshot in the dark.
The skyline glows with lit windows. One window flashes and a tiny notification pops: "Brightline Labs viewed your profile."

panels.desc: Next morning. {HERO} walks in, coffee in hand. The office lights are red. An alarm is wailing.

lines.text: WEEOO WEEOO WEEOO

panels.desc: Every screen on the floor shows the same thing: PHOENIX IS DOWN.

lines.text: DAY 19.

panels.label: wide
panels.desc: The Overlord's hologram flickers onto the wall TV, bigger than ever.

lines.text: WHO. TOUCHED. PHOENIX.

panels.label: SPLASH
panels.desc: The whole floor turns, and every single arm points at {HERO}. The four Yes-Men point in perfect sync. Captain Quick-Call points with his phone. Even a potted plant seems to lean toward them.

lines.text: Well... they own it now.
The bug was written in 2021. {HERO} joined in 2023. Details.
a fast zoom onto {HERO}'s face on "now".

panels.desc: {HERO} at their desk, the bug report on screen: "Root cause: commit a7f3e (2021)."

lines.text: This is from before I joined.
Let's not play the blame game.
(writing in his notebook) {HERO}... blame... game...

panels.desc: A glowing red ball forms above the desk: THE BLAME. It bounces menacingly. Stamped on it: "PHOENIX DOWN 🔥".

lines.text: In every office there is one ball nobody wants to hold.

items.title: BLAME PONG
items.intro: Don't let it land on you.

lines.text: {HERO} is stamped BLAMED three times. Captain Quick-Call adds a calendar event: "Phoenix Post-Mortem (presented by {HERO})".
The Blame is "shared".
In corporate, "shared blame" means it's yours, but in a group email.
The Blame ball lands on The Vendor's logo with a satisfying explosion. A Yes-Man reads aloud: "Root cause: third-party dependency." Everyone nods.

panels.desc: Night. The office is empty. {HERO} alone at their desk, the only light on the floor. Phoenix's code glows on their screen.
Close on the screen. {HERO} types fast. A new deck forms: "PHOENIX RECOVERY PLAN, by {HERO}". Diagrams, fixes, a timeline.

lines.text: If I'm going down with Phoenix, I'm going down with a plan.

panels.desc: {HERO} saves it to the team's shared drive and goes home. On the drive's file list, unnoticed, the "Viewers" icon blinks: 1 viewer.

lines.text: slow zoom on the icon.

panels.desc: Next morning. {HERO}'s phone buzzes. It's the team group chat ("Team Phoenix 🔥 Family").

panels.label: close-up
panels.desc: A screenshot posted in the chat by an unknown sender: {HERO}'s Linkd profile, with a bright green #OpenToWork frame around their photo. Below it: 12 Yes-Man emoji reactions: 👀👀👀👀👀👀👀👀👀👀👀👀
{HERO} looks up slowly. Across the floor, at an empty desk, the air ripples. The faint outline of a man in a slim blazer, smiling, then gone.

lines.text: Some villains attack you. Others just... take notes.
TO BE CONTINUED IN ISSUE #3: "DOUBLE LIFE"

items.desc: Split down the middle. Left half: {HERO} at their office desk, a forced smile, Captain Quick-Call's shadow looming. Right half: the same {HERO}, same clothes, in a glass interview room, sweating, three interviewers' silhouettes facing them. A thin crack runs between the two halves.
items.tagline: NOTICE PERIOD #3 · DOUBLE LIFE · tagline: "Nobody can know."

lines.text: PREVIOUSLY: Phoenix crashed. Everyone pointed. {HERO} wrote a recovery plan at 1 AM. And someone leaked the #OpenToWork.

panels.desc: {HERO} walks onto the floor. Conversations stop. A Yes-Man quickly turns his monitor away.
Captain Quick-Call steps into {HERO}'s path, all smiles.

lines.text: Heard you're "open to work"! Love that energy.
Hope it doesn't affect Phoenix. 🙂

panels.label: SPLASH (villain introduction)
panels.desc: THE CREDIT PHANTOM fades into view, half-transparent, by the coffee machine. Slim blazer, perfect hair, a laser pointer held like a wand. He's holding a laptop open to a slide with somebody else's name crossed out. A villain card in the corner:

lines.text: Great work is a team effort. And I'm the team.
Nobody had ever seen him do a task. Everybody had seen him present one.

card: THE CREDIT PHANTOM · Senior Associate Lead (Strategy)
Powers: Invisibility (during actual work) · Materialise (when leadership is in the room) · "As I was saying..."

panels.desc: {HERO}'s phone vibrates under the desk. An email notification: Brightline Labs: Interview invitation. Tomorrow, 3:00 PM.

lines.text: Brightline. The window that lit up.

panels.label: close-up
panels.desc: {HERO}'s face, trying very hard to look normal. A drop of sweat.

lines.text: DAY 34. Rule one of the double life: your face must say "Phoenix". Your heart may say "freedom".

panels.desc: {HERO} opens a prep doc ("Interview_prep.docx") in one tab and a fake spreadsheet in another ("Q3_final_v7_REAL.xlsx"). Over their shoulder, the open floor: people walking past, constantly.

items.title: BOSS IS COMING
items.intro: Prep for the interview. Don't get caught. Watch the reflections.

lines.text: The Credit Phantom materialises right behind {HERO}, reading the prep doc. He smiles and fades. Nothing is said. That's worse.
Mostly prepped. Captain Quick-Call caught one glimpse:
"Tell me about yourself"? ...Is that for the Phoenix retro?
...Yes.
The prep doc is complete: answers to every classic question. A Yes-Man walked past five times and saw only spreadsheets.

panels.desc: Next day. The wall clock: 2:40 PM. {HERO}, freshly ironed shirt under a hoodie, backpack ready.

lines.text: DAY 35. The interview is at 3:00. The lift is 40 metres away. Between {HERO} and the lift: everyone.

panels.desc: {HERO} types a message to Captain Quick-Call.

lines.text: Stepping out for a doctor's appointment. Back by 5.
Which doctor? 🙂

panels.desc: Bird's-eye view of the office floor, like a heist blueprint: desks, plants, the coffee machine, a printer, glass meeting rooms. Little glowing cones show where people are looking: Captain Quick-Call by the windows, Yes-Men patrolling in a line, a ripple near the pantry.

lines.text: Every heist needs a plan. {HERO} had a hoodie.

items.title: THE GREAT SNEAK
items.intro: Get to the lift. Don't get spotted. Chai Uncle knows a way.

lines.text: {HERO} arrives at Brightline 20 minutes late, out of breath.
They've... started without you. Please wait.  (the interview still happens, but the next level is harder: the tower starts with one wobbly block)
{HERO} makes the lift, but the last panel shows a Yes-Man taking a note: "14:52, lift, hoodie."
The lift doors close on {HERO}'s calm face. Through the closing gap: Captain Quick-Call, looking at an empty desk.
DING.

panels.label: wide
panels.desc: Brightline Labs. A bright, airy office. Plants that are actually alive. Natural light. Somebody laughing, genuinely.

lines.text: People... laugh here?

panels.desc: A glass interview room. THE PANEL: three interviewers in a row, lit from above like a tribunal. - Left: smiles constantly, nods at everything. - Centre: arms folded, unreadable. - Right: typing nonstop, never looks up.

lines.text: The Panel. Three judges. One verdict.
So. Tell us about yourself.
slow zoom; a heartbeat sound effect.
ba-dum. ba-dum.

items.title: TELL ME ABOUT YOURSELF
items.intro: Stack your story. Taller impresses. Wobbly topples.

lines.text: The tower topples, blocks crashing across the table. The Excel-wizard block lands in the right interviewer's coffee.
So... you were an intern?
The tower stands, swaying.
Great! We'll get back to you.
The five most dangerous words in hiring.
The tower crosses the line and glows. The centre interviewer unfolds their arms.
...When can you join?

panels.desc: 5:30 PM. {HERO} slides back into their chair at Synergex, slightly out of breath, hoodie zipped up over the interview shirt.

lines.text: DAY 35. 5:30 PM. Back before anyone noticed. Almost.

panels.desc: Captain Quick-Call appears at the partition, all smiles.

lines.text: How was the doctor?

panels.desc: {HERO} answers:

lines.text: Captain Quick-Call nods slowly, as if this means something.
...Great. Great for you.
He takes two steps back. For the next three days, nobody schedules a meeting with {HERO}.

panels.desc: A few days later. {HERO} checks email at their desk, again and again. Nothing from Brightline.

lines.text: DAY 38. Silence. In hiring, silence is a language. Nobody speaks it fluently.

panels.desc: The canteen. Chai Uncle pours {HERO} a cutting chai without being asked, then leans in.

lines.text: Your drive. The Phoenix plan. You saved it where everyone can see?
...Yes? Why?

panels.desc: Chai Uncle glances at the clock: 4:55 PM. His voice drops.

lines.text: Your deck. Boardroom. Five o'clock.
Not you presenting.

panels.label: wide
panels.desc: The boardroom at the end of the corridor. Through the glass: The Overlord's hologram hovering over the table, the Yes-Men seated in a row. At the front, the air ripples, and the Credit Phantom materialises fully, laser pointer raised.

panels.label: close-up of the screen behind him
panels.desc: The first slide: "PHOENIX RECOVERY PLAN." The author's name in the corner has been edited. {HERO}'s name is crossed out with a single digital strike. Above it, freshly typed: "by The Credit Phantom."
The Credit Phantom clears his throat.

lines.text: As I was saying...
FASCINATING. TELL ME MORE.

panels.desc: {HERO} drops their chai glass. It shatters in slow motion at their feet.

lines.text: KSSSH.
That's. My. Deck.
The clock reads 4:57. The boardroom is 120 metres away.
TO BE CONTINUED IN ISSUE #4: "DARKEST HOUR"

items.desc: The boardroom, drawn from below like a cathedral. The Credit Phantom at the head of the table, holding up {HERO}'s slide like a trophy. The Overlord's hologram applauding. In the glass door's reflection, tiny and far away, {HERO} running.
items.tagline: NOTICE PERIOD #4 · DARKEST HOUR · tagline: "Everything you built. Someone else's name."

lines.text: PREVIOUSLY: {HERO} lived a double life, faced The Panel, and came back to find their recovery plan in the Credit Phantom's hands.

panels.desc: {HERO} kicks off their shoes. Socks on the office carpet. Eyes locked on the far end of the corridor.

lines.text: Not. This. Time.

panels.label: wide, low angle
panels.desc: The corridor stretches ahead like a racetrack: wheelie chairs, a jammed printer, a crowd gathered around a birthday cake, a lift with a paper sign.

lines.text: TAK TAK TAK
fast push forward.
{HERO} arrives to applause. The Phantom is shaking hands.
WHAT A VISIONARY.
{HERO} arrives on the final slide, out of breath.
WHO IS THIS?
The author. A Yes-Man quietly opens the version history.
{HERO} bursts in with three slides to spare.
Open the version history. The Phantom freezes mid-gesture, half-transparent.

panels.label: SPLASH
panels.desc: The boardroom screen, giant: VERSION HISTORY. One line glows: "Created by {HERO} · 1:13 AM." The Credit Phantom flickers, fading in and out like a bad video call, his laser pointer drooping. The Yes-Men turn their heads toward him in perfect sync.

lines.text: I was... socialising it.
Version history. The only witness that never lies.
hold, then a glitch effect on the Phantom.

panels.desc: The Overlord's hologram leans down. For a second, it almost looks human.

lines.text: WHOEVER WROTE THIS... SHOULD STAY.
Nineteen months of silence. Then this. Now.

panels.desc: Captain Quick-Call, sweating, steps in.

lines.text: Sir, they're... serving notice.
THEN THEY HAVE PLENTY OF TIME TO TRAIN THEIR REPLACEMENT.

panels.desc: A nervous young man in a brand-new lanyard is pushed forward. Glasses, an unopened notebook, a pen still in its wrapper. This is PINTO.

lines.text: Hi! I'm Pinto. I'm your... replacement? I start today. Also I'm leaving in March. For my MBA.
DAY 41. The handover.

panels.desc: A tiny meeting room. {HERO} at a whiteboard covered in Phoenix diagrams. Pinto nodding with enormous enthusiasm, writing nothing.

lines.text: So the payroll runs on a script called test2.py—
Love that.

panels.desc: {HERO} holds up a glowing orb of light: fourteen months of knowledge. Pinto's head, in comic-style x-ray, is a sieve.

lines.text: Some handovers are a transfer. This one was a leak.

items.title: THE BRAIN DUMP
items.intro: Pour it in. Plug the leaks. Nothing he forgets is your fault. (It will be.)

lines.text: Pinto's notebook has one line: "test2.py = ???". Captain Quick-Call adds a calendar event: "KT Part 2 (and 3, 4, 5...)."
Pinto understands most of it.
Quick question. What does Phoenix do?
Pinto's head glows.
I... I understand Phoenix.
He would forget it all by March. But not on {HERO}'s watch.

panels.desc: Night. {HERO}'s flat. The phone buzzes on the table: an unknown number. The room goes dark around it. The trench-coat silhouette returns, lit only by the city behind.

lines.text: {HERO}. Brightline Labs would like to make you an offer.
DAY 47.
Before we do. One small question.
What's your... expected CTC?

panels.desc: Between them, the table turns into a green felt card table. Chips appear. The Recruiter shuffles a deck with one hand.

lines.text: FRRRRP
Every salary negotiation is a game of cards. Only one side admits it.

items.title: THE NUMBER
items.intro: Play your cards. Read their tells. Don't push until they fold.

lines.text: The Recruiter stands, buttons the trench coat.
We'll... keep you on file.
The envelope arrives, a little thinner.
It's our best offer. (It isn't.)
The Recruiter slides an envelope across the felt. It glows like a sacred artefact.
Welcome to Brightline.

panels.label: SPLASH
panels.desc: {HERO} alone in the dark flat, holding the offer letter. Light pours out of the envelope onto their face. Behind them, on the wall, the shadows of every villain so far, cast long and huge, then shrinking.

lines.text: I got it.
After 212 applications, 9 calls, 4 rounds and one stolen deck... a door.

panels.label: close-up of the letter
panels.desc: "Joining date: 15 days from today."

lines.text: DAY 48. Notice period remaining: 42 days.

panels.desc: {HERO} counts on their fingers, twice.

lines.text: Fifteen... forty-two...

panels.desc: The flat's lights flicker. A cold draft. Laminated pages drift through the air like falling leaves. In the doorway, impossibly, Madame Policy.

lines.text: Policy.
Is.
Policy.
TO BE CONTINUED IN ISSUE #5: "THE GREAT ESCAPE"

panels.desc: {HERO} alone, staring at a silent phone. The "On file" folder icon on screen grows until it fills the panel.

lines.text: The offer didn't come. Not this time.

panels.desc: The canteen. Chai Uncle slides over a chai and a crumpled paper napkin with a phone number on it.

lines.text: My nephew's company. They interview tomorrow. Don't tell them about the samosa incident.
What samosa incident?
Exactly.

panels.desc: A new glass room. A new Panel of three, even more unreadable.

lines.text: Tell us about yourself. And this time... impress us.
One last shot. The tower must stand.

items.desc: {HERO} mid-leap through a giant window made of red tape, glass shards of policy pages flying, the offer letter clutched to their chest like a shield. Below, Madame Policy reaching up. Above, a sunrise.
items.tagline: NOTICE PERIOD #5 · THE GREAT ESCAPE · tagline: "Fifteen days. Forty-two days. One way out."

lines.text: PREVIOUSLY: {HERO} beat the Phantom, poured Phoenix into Pinto, and won the offer. Joining date: 15 days. Notice left: 42.

panels.desc: Madame Policy's office. Filing cabinets to the ceiling. A single plant, laminated.

lines.text: Early release requires: manager approval, a completed handover, no dues from six departments, and... my signature.
And if I have all of that?
Then we'll discuss.

panels.desc: She hands over a form. It unfolds, and unfolds, and unfolds, all the way to the floor. At the top: NO-DUES CLEARANCE · FORM 7B.

lines.text: FWUP FWUP FWUP

panels.label: bird's-eye
panels.desc: The office floor, drawn like a board game: six desks marked IT, ADMIN, FINANCE, FACILITIES, LIBRARY (?), and HR. Lanes between them full of moving trolleys, a cleaning robot, and a Fun Friday conga line.

lines.text: DAY 50. Six signatures. One laptop. A floor that never stops moving.

panels.desc: {HERO} hugs the laptop, the charger, the ID card, and a mysterious dongle.

lines.text: What is this dongle?
Return it. Nobody knows. Return it.

items.title: NO-DUES CROSSING
items.intro: Cross the floor. Get the signatures. Don't drop the laptop.

lines.text: {HERO} drops the dongle into the cleaning robot. It beeps triumphantly and drives away.
The dongle was never seen again. Its cost was added to the final settlement.
Five of six. Finance's stamp reads "PENDING (SYSTEM DOWN)". It counts. Barely.
Form 7B complete, all six stamps glowing. Even the Library signed. (There was a library.)

panels.desc: {HERO} at their desk, typing the farewell email. Calm. Almost peaceful.

lines.text: DAY 55. The farewell email. The last thing anyone here will read from you. They'll only read the subject line.

panels.label: close-up
panels.desc: The subject line: "Moving on 🙏". {HERO}'s finger hovers over the To: field. It auto-fills: ALL-STAFF (4,312 recipients).

lines.text: Wait. Wait wait wait—
CLICK.

panels.label: wide
panels.desc: Across the whole tower, 4,312 screens light up at once. A low rumble.

lines.text: RRRRRRRRMBL
Somewhere, someone pressed Reply All.

items.title: REPLY-ALL STORM
items.intro: 4,312 recipients. One Mute button. Hold the line.

lines.text: The mail server crashes. The Overlord's hologram flickers: WHO DID THIS? Every arm points, one last time.
The storm settles at 237 replies.
Three people unsubscribed from the company.
Inbox: zero. A single reply survives, from Chai Uncle: "Come for one last chai."

panels.desc: The Reply-All storm finally settles. {HERO} grabs the backpack and heads for the exit. The corridor is empty. Too empty.

lines.text: DAY 56. 6:58 PM. Two minutes to freedom.

panels.label: wide
panels.desc: At the glass exit door, a silhouette. Phone in hand. Lanyard swinging like a pendulum. Captain Quick-Call.

lines.text: Leaving without our one last quick call?
CLICK.

panels.label: close-up
panels.desc: {HERO} drops the backpack and rolls up their sleeves.

lines.text: I'm off the clock.
Nobody is ever off the clock.

panels.label: SPLASH
panels.desc: The two face off in the empty office. Cubicle walls form an arena. The green EXIT sign glows behind the Captain. The fluorescent lights flicker like a stadium.

lines.text: Every hero gets one fair fight.
ROUND 1 · FIGHT!

items.title: ONE LAST QUICK CALL
items.intro: He's blocking the exit. Punch, kick, block, and charge up your resignation letter.

lines.text: The Captain dusts off his shirt and sends a fresh invite: "Q1 Planning (owner: {HERO})".
See you Monday!
{HERO} wins, barely, collar askew. The Captain picks up his phone and pretends he was leaving anyway.
Good chat.
K.O.! Captain Quick-Call's phone skids across the carpet. The screen reads "Call ended · 0:47".
...Let's circle back. Never.

panels.desc: The canteen, last chai. Chai Uncle pours the long golden arc one final time.

lines.text: Twenty-two years, many people left. Few left well.
She's waiting for you. Remember: everything she says is policy. So ask to see the policy.

panels.desc: {HERO} drinks the chai in one go. Puts the glass down. Stands.

lines.text: DAY 58. Joining date: in 5 days. Notice remaining: 32.
tok.

panels.label: SPLASH (final boss)
panels.desc: Madame Policy's office has become a fortress. Filing cabinets tower like castle walls. Laminated pages swirl around her in a hurricane. Her stamp glows red. Her glasses flash white. A villain card, upgraded:

lines.text: Ninety days is ninety days.
Then show me where it says that.
shake; the page border turns red.

card: Powers: PDF Barrage · "As Per Process" Shield · The Pen That Never Signs
Weakness: "Can you show me where it says that?"

items.title: THE RELIEVING LETTER
items.intro: Three phases. One signature. Your new life is on the other side.

lines.text: The pen escapes out of the window.
Policy is policy. The joining date passes.
Signed, with an asterisk: "*Subject to F&F in 45 working days."
I'll take it.
The pen touches paper. The signature glows. The fortress collapses into a single tidy desk.
...The clause was never there. Nobody ever asked.

panels.label: close-up
panels.desc: The relieving letter, signed. {HERO} reads it, smiling, then stops.

lines.text: "Dear [FIRST_NAME], we wish you all the best at [COMPANY]."
...Close enough.

panels.desc: {HERO} walks out of the Synergex tower for the last time. The doors slide shut behind them. The lanyard stays on the security desk.

lines.text: DAY 60. Relieved.

panels.label: SPLASH (epilogue)
panels.desc: Brightline Labs, morning. Sunlight across a desk. A real plant. A real chair. A welcome card signed by people who actually wrote messages. {HERO} sits down, closes their eyes, and breathes.

lines.text: Day one. Of something else.

panels.desc: The screen goes black. Small white text: "After the credits..."
{HERO}'s new laptop. A chat notification slides in from {HERO}'s new manager.

lines.text: Hey! Welcome aboard! 🎉
PING!
Got 5 mins? 🙂
THE END...?

panels.label: SPLASH
panels.desc: Day 90. {HERO} walks out of the Synergex tower with a cardboard box. No offer. Rain. The Escapee's glowing post floats above, out of reach. On their phone, Linkd updates their headline on its own: "Exploring Opportunities ✨".

lines.text: No offer by Day 90. The Hunt goes on, but this story ends here.
GAME OVER · Try again from this Issue.

panels.label: SPLASH
panels.desc: Madame Policy stamps a single sheet: TERMINATED. The Yes-Men point in perfect sync. Captain Quick-Call smiles, phone in hand.

lines.text: Since you're leaving anyway... we thought we'd help.
Blame full. No relieving letter. No background check will clear.
GAME OVER · Try again from this Issue.

panels.label: SPLASH
panels.desc: The offer letter in {HERO}'s hands crumbles into ash. The Recruiter's silhouette turns away.

lines.text: We've decided to move ahead with another candidate.
The joining date beat the exit date.
GAME OVER · Try again from this Issue.
